THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON 29.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 M.A.C.A.No.651 of 2020  2  2025:KER:72905  C.S.SUDHA, J.

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1934/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 21/05/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 15/07/2017 at 01:30 p.m., while he was riding scooter bearing registration no.KL-11-AV-3151 from Idiyangara to Mankavu and when he reached at Pushpa junction, lorry bearing registration no.KL-58-3677 driven by the second respondent in a rash and 2025:KER:72905 negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent-owner and the second respondent-driver of the offending vehicle filed written statement denying negligence on the part of the latter.
The amount claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
4. The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent.

The averments in the petition regarding age, occupation,
income and injuries sustained to the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was contended that the lorry did not have valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of the accident.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A12 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Exts.B1 and B2 were marked on the side of the 1st respondent and Exts.B3 was marked on the side of the 2025:KER:72905 third respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the Abdul Khader vs United India Insurance Co.Ltd on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99022590/
2 incident and hence awarded an amount of 2,09,500/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

sentences.text:
Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Multiplier
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that as the latter was 52 years old, the multiplier to be 2025:KER:72905 applied is '11'.
However, the Tribunal has wrongly applied 9.
This submission is not opposed by the learned counsel for the third respondent-insurer.

Hence, the multiplier to be applied shall be '11'.
Pain and suffering 10.
An amount of 50,000/- was claimed.
However, the Tribunal granted an amount of 15,000/-, which is contended to be on the lower side.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in paragraph 11 of the impugned Award, the Tribunal has stated that "petitioner suffered comminuted fracture base of 1st metatarsal with depressed fragment/shaft of 2nd and 3rd metatarsal left foot."
That being the position, the amount awarded is on the lower side and hence same needs to be appropriately enhanced.
11. Ext.A2 wound certificate reads thus- " Running over (Lt) foot  C/o pain in (Lt) foot, difficulty walk/stand.

No C/o LOC,
ENT bleed.
2025: KER:72905 O/E: Tenderness, Deformity, ROM (+) over (Lt) foot on dorsal surface.
Abrasion over (Rt) extensor surface of hand behind (Rt) elbow.
Abrasion on (Lt) foot over lateral surface of Great toe & (Rt) knee."
It is not discernible from the impugned Award as to how the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the claim petitioner had suffered a fracture as stated in paragraph 11 of the impugned Award.
The learned counsel for the claim petitioner is also unable to point out any other document(s) which would show that the claim petitioner had sustained a fracture.

As Ext.A2 does not refer to any fracture, I find the amount awarded by the Tribunal in the light of the injuries sustained as noted in Ext.A2 to be just and reasonable and hence does not call for any interference.

12. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:

The third respondent/
insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period 2025:KER:72905 of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
